column1: DEJ is prime, TYBMS is the subcontractor
column3: Furukawa Denki has backed out and does not witness. DEJ submits the proposal and holds the main contract. TYBMS is subcontracted to DEJ for the BMS work: design, programming, installation supervision and commissioning. Stage gates that Furukawa would have signed are accepted by DEJ. Hotel operations still accept the plant back to automatic control.

Fabrication, cabling, installation, instrumentation and programming are overlapping phases of one continuous delivery. The elapsed duration is still nine months. The completion date is the contract date plus nine months. Moving the contract date moves the whole programme. It does not lengthen it.

column1: Programs still have to exist before the factory loads them
column3: Bench loading still happens in months C+3 to C+5, and it still needs the application programs. Under one contract that is a sequence, not a second award: authoring starts in month C+1. If the programs are not ready, reduce the factory step to a harness test and load every program on site. That adds about an hour per panel to a night that has no spare hour.

Panel replacement, instruments and the program download still meet inside one night, 67 times. They are stages of the same contract now, so there is no second contract to wait for at 03:00. DEJ names the person who makes the 05:00 GO/NO-GO. TYBMS makes the technical recommendation.

column1: The contract date sets the season, not the duration
column3: Controller lead is still 12–16 weeks, and the purchase order still has to go out about a month after the contract date. The cutover is months C+6 and C+7. If the contract date is early October, those months are the April–May shoulder season. A later contract date keeps the nine months and lands the cutover later in the year, possibly in cooling season. The duration is not stretched to chase the shoulder season. The next comfortable slot after a missed shoulder season is about a year later, which means a later contract date, not a longer project.

column1: IEIEJ p-A may force new device-network cabling
column3: The 2002 trunk drawing says IPEV-S 0.9 mm². The installed Azbil cable may be IEIEJ p-A. That cable is not reused unless a test shows it meets the new network specification. New cabling is surveyed in month C+0, designed with the panel drawings, and pulled during the fabrication window so each wave lands on a segment that is already proved. Finding IEIEJ p-A on the cutover night is the failure this phase exists to prevent. It does not add a month.

Every quantity here is derived from panels_schedule.json, but the durations are planning estimates. 3–5 h to transfer a panel's terminations and 4–8 h to function-test it are the two that set the night window — have the installer confirm both against their own productivity figures before the waves are fixed.

column1: Instrumentation may not need a full replacement
column3: The instrument phase assumes all 591 analog devices are replaced. If as-found calibration shows a population that is still within tolerance, that work shrinks to verification and re-ranging. Survey a sample before that scope is frozen inside the single contract.
